annotation.title_clean: Industrial Robot Ethics: The Challenges of Closer Human Collaboration in Future Manufacturing Systems
annotation.title_en: Industrial Robot Ethics: The Challenges of Closer Human Collaboration in Future Manufacturing Systems
annotation.venue: A World with Robots: International Conference on Robot Ethics (ICRE 2015), Springer
annotation.summary_en: Conference chapter on ethical issues arising as Industrie 4.0 brings industrial robots out of cages into close collaboration with workers. It argues that beyond physical safety, psychological harm, worker acceptance, trust, training and data capture for monitoring need ethical attention.
key_provisions_or_claims: Human-robot collaboration shifts ethical concern from physical guarding to psychological harm and anxiety.
Workers' views on 'safe' collisions at accepted impact levels are poorly understood.
Ethical protection of operators should be built into training and organisational interventions.
Adaptive, more autonomous robots require workers to adapt their own behaviour.
Greater data capture for performance monitoring raises ethical issues.
